messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm seeing a gap in KMS-related audit events between 02:00 and 02:12 UTC last night. Snapshots restored during that window don't show Decrypt events in CloudTrail. Did anyone touch RBAC or logging pipelines around that maintenance window?

olivia: i just deployed the uploader-role tidy (removed legacy grants) at 01:58 — shouldn't affect CloudTrail itself but could affect who can request decrypts. which snapshots are missing entries?

maria: tenant-snap-20260314-02:05 is the main one. We have S3 objects with SSE-KMS metadata but no corresponding KMS:Decrypt entries. local DB snapshots show restore succeeded though.

todd: two quick angles: 1) audit ingestion (CloudTrail -> ES/Lambda) might have backfilled/dlq issues, 2) KMS grants/ephemeral grants TTL got changed in the RBAC sweep. KMS still returns ciphertext -> if grants were absent maybe decrypts used a different workflow (e.g., envelope decrypt done by an upload service with re-encryption).

sam: i'll check the ingest lambda DLQ and the ES index latency. if CloudTrail events were dropped they'd show in the DLQ or in S3 bucket with raw logs.

aws-ci: deploy completed: uploader-serviceaccount-role-change @01:58 UTC by olivia (rev 84f3).

olivia: i removed a stale iam:PassRole mapping and rotated a role binding — i can revert but need to know if that's the cause. that role had a grant-forwarder tag we used for temporary grants.

maria: can someone run a raw CloudTrail lookup for Decrypt events around that timestamp? i tried `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-14T01:50:00Z --end-time 2026-03-14T02:20:00Z` and got fewer events than expected.

olivia: try filtering by ResourceName (CMK id) too — sometimes lookup-events omits kms:Decrypt if you don't include the key id.

olivia: example query:```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
```

todd: also check CloudTrail event sampling and Insights. If the ingestion tier hit a rate limit, CloudTrail can sample or throttle non-ReadOnly events in the Insights flow. we've had one case where high PutObject churn caused KMS-related events to be sampled.

maria: how do we differentiate sampling vs dropped-by-ingest?

todd: sampling will still leave raw S3 logs in the CloudTrail bucket. DLQ/drop means the lambda that parses them failed. check S3 prefix `AWSLogs/123456789012/CloudTrail/us-west-2/2026/03/14/` for objects during 02:00-02:20.

sam: DLQ is empty but I see a backlog of unprocessed S3 objects in the analytics bucket for that hour — `cloudtrail-raw/2026/03/14/02/`. processing lambda logs show several `ThrottlingException` errors hitting the downstream ES endpoint.

olivia: that explains ingestion delay. events probably arrived late so the quick lookup missed them if you queried our ES index. maria, try the raw S3 objects or wait for backfill.

maria: raw S3 logs do contain KMS Decrypt events for tenant-snap-20260314-02:05 — they just weren't indexed in the observable dashboards. thanks. question: do we need to revert my RBAC change? it removed a temporary grant tag that allowed uploader-side re-encryption; if that's gone restores might silently use a different code path.

todd: don't revert yet. action items: 1) sam/ops to finish backfill and reindex (priority) 2) security to run a grant-scan for ephemeral grants and TTLs (todd) 3) eng to audit uploader codepath for envelope decrypt vs server-side decrypt (olivia) 4) open incident if any tenant data access is suspected.

sam: starting reindex job now. ETA ~20m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — id INC-2026-0314-07 by sam for delayed audit ingestion. severity: low, owner: eng-security.

maria: pinging @sam and @todd — once reindex is done can we confirm there were no unauthorized decrypts (i.e., events show principal=upload-service-account only)? if we see anonymous or unexpected principals we escalate.

olivia: i'll also push a quick smoke to the uploader in staging to validate grant propagation and TTL handling.

todd: i'll run a one-off KMS grant TTL audit:`python tools/kms_grant_scan.py --window 30d --report /tmp/grants-03014.csv` and post results. keep an eye on any grants with TTL > 7d or missing principal tags.

sam: reindex finished — dashboards updated. KMS Decrypt events present and principals look like `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/upload-service/instance-...` only. no unexpected principals.

maria: that's a relief. final ask: can we add a sentinel monitor for CloudTrail indexing lag (>5m) and a runbook step to check for KMS grant-tag drift after role edits?

olivia: yes, i'll add a monitor and a quick checklist in the RBAC change playbook.

todd: i'll add the grant-scan output to periodic security reports and add an audit rule for missing `grant:source=rbac-scan` tag.

maria: thanks all — closing thread unless anyone sees additional anomalies. :thumbsup:
